headings.reviewNote: Requires operators to collect $1.50 per ton at sanitary landfills and $1.00 per ton at demolition landfills (with CPI adjustments restricted during 2005-2027) for deposit in the Solid Waste Management Fund.

headings.title: Department rulemaking for fee collection and transmittal
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to establish administrative rules governing the collection and transmittal of fees.

headings.title: Separate fee enumeration and collection cost retention
headings.reviewNote: Requires separate fee enumeration on invoices, permits pass-throughs, and allows collection cost retention.

headings.title: Department audits of landfill records and fees
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department audits of financial and operating records to verify fee collections and transmittals.

headings.title: Mandatory tonnage fee on transfer station waste
headings.reviewNote: Requires transfer station operators to transmit a $1.50 per ton fee on solid waste accepted for out-of-state disposal, exempting stations solely separating materials for recycling or resource recovery.

headings.title: Designation of up to two free disposal days
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes political subdivisions operating disposal areas to designate up to two free disposal days annually.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsections for 260.330 establishing state solid waste landfill and transfer station fees, audits, and free disposal days.

headings.title: Annual appropriation for recovered material market development
headings.reviewNote: Allocates $800,000 annually upon appropriation for recovered material market development and up to $200,000 annually for grants to districts receiving fewer funds than under August 27, 2004 criteria.

headings.title: Formula allocation for dump cleanup and grants
headings.reviewNote: Allocates 39% of remaining fund revenues to the department for illegal disposal elimination, permitting, and grants (plus 2005-2027 fee increases) and 61% to solid waste districts by population and revenue with minimum allocations and five-year reversion.

headings.title: Advisory board recommendations for grant allocation criteria
headings.reviewNote: Directs the advisory board to recommend criteria prioritizing waste reduction and recycling grant proposals.

headings.title: Non-supplanting requirement for district grant funds
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits using district grant funds to supplant existing local government solid waste appropriations.

headings.title: District grant applications and department compliance verification
headings.reviewNote: Requires districts to submit grant applications and documentation verifying notice and eligibility to the department.

headings.title: State security interest in grant-funded equipment
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to secure a security interest in all equipment purchased with state grant funds.

headings.title: Ten percent interest on delinquent fee transmittals
headings.reviewNote: Imposes ten percent annual interest on late fee transmittals deposited into the solid waste management fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsections for 260.335 directing distribution of solid waste fund moneys, market development allocations, and grant administration.

headings.title: Establishment and composition of Solid Waste Advisory Board
headings.reviewNote: Creates the advisory board composed of district executive board chairmen and appointed industry members.

headings.title: Advisory board reports to general assembly committees
headings.reviewNote: Directs the advisory board to prepare reports on solid waste issues for legislative standing committees.

headings.title: Quarterly regular meetings and special meeting notices
headings.reviewNote: Requires quarterly meetings, specifies quorum rules, and sets procedures for calling special meetings.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 260.345 establishing the Solid Waste Advisory Board, legislative reporting, and quarterly meetings.

headings.title: Creation and membership of Hazardous Waste Commission
headings.reviewNote: Creates the seven-member Hazardous Waste Management Commission appointed by the governor.

headings.title: Four-year terms of office and vacancy appointments
headings.reviewNote: Establishes staggered four-year terms of office and procedures for filling commissioner vacancies.

headings.title: Quarterly commission meetings, notice requirements, and quorum
headings.reviewNote: Mandates at least four regular meetings annually, public notice, and a four-member quorum.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 260.365 establishing the Hazardous Waste Management Commission, member qualifications, terms, and meetings.

headings.title: Promotion of hazardous waste recycling and treatment
headings.reviewNote: Requires the commission to encourage recycling, detoxification, and treatment over land disposal.

headings.title: Waste categorization, inspection frequency, and facility fees
headings.reviewNote: Directs categorizing hazardous waste by toxicity and characteristics, setting inspection frequencies, and establishing commercial off-site facility inspection fees capped at $12,000 annually with a 45-day accounting and refund rule.

headings.title: Commission powers to adopt standards and rules
headings.reviewNote: Grants comprehensive rulemaking, licensing, inspection, and hearing powers to the commission.

headings.title: Administrative procedure compliance for commission rules
headings.reviewNote: Conditions effectiveness of hazardous waste rules on compliance with statutory administrative procedures.

headings.title: Precedence of hazardous waste section for remediation
headings.reviewNote: Resolves statutory conflicts by giving precedence to this section for risk-based remediation rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 260.370 governing Hazardous Waste Management Commission powers, waste categorization, rulemaking, and risk-based rules.

headings.title: Contracts promoting hazardous waste reduction and recycling
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to enter into contracts for projects promoting hazardous waste reduction and recycling.

headings.title: Participation in regional waste exchange clearinghouses
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to establish or participate in regional waste exchange clearinghouses.

headings.title: Advisory duties regarding low-level radioactive waste compact
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to advise Missouri's member on the Midwest Low-Level Radioactive Waste Commission.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 260.372 authorizing recycling promotion contracts, waste exchange clearinghouses, and low-level compact advice.

headings.title: Prohibition on rules stricter than federal regulations
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the commission from promulgating rules stricter than federal Title 40 CFR regulations.

headings.title: Preservation of other statutory enforcement authorities
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that the section does not repeal other laws and preserves commission and department authority to implement and enforce other statutes and rules.

headings.title: Nullification of inconsistent rules on December 31, 2017
headings.reviewNote: Declares specified Title 10 CSR Division 25 rules inconsistent with subsection 1 or imposing mandatory obligations beyond federal 40 CFR rules null and void on December 31, 2017, with the least stringent rule controlling.

headings.title: No automatic permit modification; modification upon request
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that the section does not effectuate a permit modification, but requires the department upon request to modify permits containing requirements no longer in effect.

headings.title: Prohibition on excluding commission rules from EPA packages
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the department from selectively excluding any commission-promulgated rule from EPA authorization application packages or program revisions under 40 CFR 271.5 or 271.21.

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking compliance and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Conditions rule effectiveness on chapter 536 compliance and establishes nonseverability invalidating rulemaking authority and rules after August 28, 2012, if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsections for 260.373 restricting hazardous waste rulemaking to federal stringency limits, preserving other laws, nullifying inconsistent rules, modifying permits, barring EPA exclusions, and requiring chapter 536 compliance.

headings.title: Mandatory generator registration, manifests, and fee payments
headings.reviewNote: Requires Missouri hazardous waste generators to register ($100 initial/renewal fee), containerize, manifest, report, allow inspections, and pay $5/ton fees ($150 min to $52,000 max), with commission fee-revision authority expiring August 28, 2030.

headings.title: Annual fee on out-of-state hazardous waste
headings.reviewNote: Imposes a two-dollar per ton fee on hazardous waste received by Missouri facilities from outside the state.

headings.title: Small quantity exemptions for households and farmers
headings.reviewNote: Exempts individual householders, farmers, and infrequent small quantity generators from section requirements while requiring safe management and compliance with special management notices.

headings.title: Late payment penalty and expiration of fees
headings.reviewNote: Imposes a fifteen percent late payment penalty and sets December 31, 2018 expiration for the prescribed fee while preserving collection for waste generated and reported prior to that date.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 260.380 governing generator registration, manifest tracking, out-of-state waste fees, and small quantity exemptions.

headings.title: Mandatory facility permits, manifests, and monitoring reports
headings.reviewNote: Requires facility owners to obtain operating permits, maintain manifest systems, and report monitoring data.

headings.title: Two percent state tax on gross disposal charges
headings.reviewNote: Requires hazardous waste landfills to collect a two percent state tax on gross disposal charges.

headings.title: Mandatory facility closure and postclosure financial assurance
headings.reviewNote: Requires facility operators to properly close sites and maintain financial assurance for postclosure care.

headings.title: Commercial facility inspection fees established by rule
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to establish annual inspection fees for commercial hazardous waste facilities.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 260.390 governing hazardous waste facility operating permits, gross charge taxes, closure plans, and inspection fees.

headings.title: Creation and revenue sources of Hazardous Waste Fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Hazardous Waste Fund supported by fees, taxes, penalties, and donations for hazardous waste, tank, and Superfund programs; source notes section 260.037 was repealed in 2007 and subdivision (7) transfers cease August 28, 2025.

headings.title: Non-reversion and investment of unexpended fund balance
headings.reviewNote: Exempts the Hazardous Waste Fund from section 33.080 general revenue transfers except by appropriation and requires investing unexpended balances to generate fund income.

headings.title: Creation of Hazardous Waste Facility Inspection Subaccount
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Hazardous Waste Facility Inspection Subaccount within the fund to receive facility inspection fees and fund department compliance inspections.

headings.title: Transfer of remaining hazardous waste remedial fund balance
headings.reviewNote: Transfers the remaining balance of the hazardous waste remedial fund into the Hazardous Waste Fund.

headings.title: Prerequisite voluntary agreement efforts before cleanup use
headings.reviewNote: Bars using fund moneys for abandoned site cleanup unless the director has made all reasonable efforts to secure voluntary payment agreements from responsible persons.

headings.title: Director duty to recover expended cleanup funds
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to make all reasonable efforts to recover expended cleanup funds through litigation or cooperative agreements and deposit recoveries into the Hazardous Waste Fund.

headings.title: Annual general revenue request for CERCLA state match
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to request an annual general revenue appropriation equal to any state match obligation to the EPA for CERCLA cleanups.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsections for 260.391 creating the Hazardous Waste Fund, non-reversion, inspection subaccount, remedial fund transfer, voluntary cleanup efforts, cost recovery, and CERCLA state match requests.

headings.title: Definitions for radioactive waste shipment fee provisions
headings.reviewNote: Defines cask, high-level, highway route controlled quantity, low-level, shipper, spent nuclear fuel, state-funded higher education institutions, and transuranic waste; source footnote notes section 260.399 does not exist.

headings.title: Per-shipment fees for transporting radioactive waste through state
headings.reviewNote: Establishes truck ($1,800 plus $25/mile over 200 miles), rail ($1,300 first cask, $125 additional), and low-level ($125) shipment fees while exempting state-funded higher education institutions (which reimburse highway patrol escort costs).

headings.title: Deposit of fees and authorized radiation monitoring uses
headings.reviewNote: Directs depositing shipment fees into the environmental radiation monitoring fund for inspections, escorts, emergency response coordination, responder training and equipment, remediation oversight, and agency administrative costs.

headings.title: Reimbursement of other state agencies from monitoring fund
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that other state agencies may receive reimbursement from the department and environmental radiation monitoring fund for services achieving section objectives.

headings.title: Pro rata shipper refunds when fund balance exceeds $300,000
headings.reviewNote: Requires returning any unencumbered environmental radiation monitoring fund balance exceeding three hundred thousand dollars in a fiscal year to shippers pro rata.

headings.title: Interagency rulemaking authority and chapter 536 rules
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department, coordinating with health and public safety departments, to promulgate rules subject to chapter 536 compliance and nonseverability after August 28, 2009.

headings.title: Appropriation of deposited fees and interest accrual
headings.reviewNote: Provides that deposited shipment fees shall be used subject to appropriation for administration and enforcement, with all earned interest accruing to the fund.

headings.title: Pre-shipment payment requirement for transport fees
headings.reviewNote: Requires all radioactive waste transport fees to be paid to the department of natural resources prior to shipment.

headings.title: Advance written notice of radioactive waste shipments
headings.reviewNote: Requires shippers to provide advance written notice of radioactive material shipments to state officials.

headings.title: Civil penalties for notice or payment failure
headings.reviewNote: Imposes civil penalties up to ten times the assessed fee for failing to pay or provide advance notice.

headings.title: Biennial department report to general assembly on fund
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to submit biennial reports to the general assembly detailing fund activities.

headings.title: Exemption for military and defense radioactive shipments
headings.reviewNote: Exempts shipments conducted by or for the federal government for military defense purposes.

headings.title: Statutory sunset date for radioactive monitoring program
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that the radioactive waste monitoring program automatically sunsets on August 28, 2030.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 13 subsections for 260.392 defining radioactive waste terms, imposing shipment fees, directing fund uses and shipper refunds, authorizing rules, requiring advance notices, penalties, reports, and sunset.

headings.title: Exemption for on-site management and out-of-state transport
headings.reviewNote: Exempts generator on-site waste management and out-of-state transport from treatment technology rules.

headings.title: Mandatory use of best demonstrated available technology
headings.reviewNote: Requires generators to use best demonstrated available technology for treatment before landfill disposal.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 260.393 exempting on-site management and mandating best available technology for hazardous waste treatment.

headings.title: Ban on untreated disposal and on-site or slag exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Exempts generator on-site storage/treatment, historic smelter slag disposal, and out-of-state transport, and prohibits disposing of untreated hazardous waste in permitted Missouri disposal facilities after August 13, 1988.

headings.title: Proof of investigated landfill alternatives prior to disposal
headings.reviewNote: Requires generators to demonstrate that landfill alternatives were investigated prior to disposal.

headings.title: Commission determination of best demonstrated available technology
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to determine best demonstrated available technology standards for disposal facilities.

headings.title: Prohibition on impermissible waste dilution to avoid listing
headings.reviewNote: Provides that hazardous waste diluted below threshold levels remains listed unless part of manufacturing.

headings.title: Inapplicability to state registry or Superfund sites
headings.reviewNote: Exempts abandoned registry sites and federal Superfund sites from disposal technology restrictions.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 260.394 restricting untreated hazardous waste landfilling, requiring alternatives reviews, and prohibiting dilution.

headings.title: Mandatory transporter license requirement for waste hauling
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits transporting hazardous waste in Missouri without obtaining a department transporter license.

headings.title: Transporter license application review and vehicle safety standards
headings.reviewNote: Directs license issuance upon verifying that applicant equipment complies with federal and state rules.

headings.title: Grounds for transporter license suspension or revocation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes license suspension or revocation for operating in violation of standards or endangering health.

headings.title: Administrative appeal procedures for transporter license decisions
headings.reviewNote: Provides thirty-day administrative appeal rights before the administrative hearing commission.

headings.title: One-year license term and annual renewal requirements
headings.reviewNote: Sets a one-year transporter license duration renewable upon demonstration of continued compliance.

headings.title: License exemption for on-site transport across property
headings.reviewNote: Exempts on-site transport or transport between contiguous generator properties from licensing.

headings.title: Mandatory permit requirement for hazardous waste facilities
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits constructing, altering, or operating a hazardous waste facility without a valid permit.

headings.title: Public notice and advertising for proposed permits
headings.reviewNote: Requires department public notice, news releases, and local official notification for proposed permits.

headings.title: Facility permit issuance, terms, conditions, and supervision
headings.reviewNote: Directs permit issuance within 180 days with necessary testing and supervision conditions, or a written denial report; source footnote notes word 'and' appears in original rolls ('one hundred * eighty days').

headings.title: Grounds for facility permit suspension or revocation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes permit suspension or revocation for violations, health threats, or public nuisances.

headings.title: Administrative appeal procedures for facility permit actions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes aggrieved persons to appeal permit decisions to the administrative hearing commission.

headings.title: Fixed permit term limit not exceeding ten years
headings.reviewNote: Limits facility permits to fixed terms up to ten years and requires renewal reviews of new technology.

headings.title: Permit exemptions for storage, POTWs, and resource recovery
headings.reviewNote: Exempts rule-exempted on-site storage, permitted publicly owned treatment works under section 644.051, certified resource recovery facilities, and resource recovery portions of dual-use facilities from facility permits.

headings.title: Exempted facility compliance and resource recovery certification
headings.reviewNote: Requires exempted facilities to comply with section 260.390(3)-(7) and generator recordkeeping, and requires resource recovery facilities to apply for certification with plans, $500/$1,000 application fees, and cost reimbursement.

headings.title: Interim status authorizations for pre-existing facilities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes pre-existing facilities with federal interim status to continue operations under Part A.

headings.title: Prohibition on denying permits based on market need
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits denying transporter licenses or facility permits solely due to lack of public or market need.

headings.title: Mandatory leachate collection systems for new landfills
headings.reviewNote: Requires leachate collection systems for landfills constructed after October 1980 and protects aquifers.

headings.title: Annual transportation fee for railroad corporations
headings.reviewNote: Imposes an annual fee of $350 on railroad corporations transporting hazardous waste or substances.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 18 subsections for 260.395 governing transporter licenses, facility permits, public hearings, appeals, and landfill liner rules.

headings.title: Definitions of polychlorinated biphenyls and PCB facilities
headings.reviewNote: Defines PCB substances at fifty parts per million or above and defines commercial PCB facilities.

headings.title: Mandatory hazardous waste or federal TSCA permits
headings.reviewNote: Requires commercial PCB facilities to hold state hazardous waste permits or federal TSCA permits.

headings.title: Department duty to maintain list of PCB facilities
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of natural resources to compile and maintain a list of all commercial PCB facilities.

headings.title: Compliance transition deadline and letters of intent
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a 120-day compliance schedule and letter of intent procedure for existing facilities.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 260.396 defining polychlorinated biphenyls, regulating commercial PCB facilities, and setting compliance deadlines.

headings.title: Mandatory party attendance, oaths, and stenographic transcripts
headings.reviewNote: Requires party attendance, sworn testimony, and stenographic recording at commission public hearings.

headings.title: Subpoena powers, oaths, and civil discovery rules
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes subpoenas, witness oaths, and applies standard civil discovery rules to commission hearings.

headings.title: Quorum for rulemaking and appointment of hearing officers
headings.reviewNote: Requires four commissioners for rulemaking hearings and authorizes hearing officers for contested cases.

headings.title: Written approval by four commissioners for final orders
headings.reviewNote: Requires written approval by four commissioners for final orders after reviewing the full record.

headings.title: Advance notice and public hearing procedures for rules
headings.reviewNote: Specifies thirty-day notice, press releases, and public hearing procedures for adopting standards or rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 260.400 governing public hearing procedures, subpoenas, hearing officers, final orders, and rulemaking hearings.

headings.title: Commission authority to grant individual variances upon proof
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes individual variances from hazardous waste requirements upon proof that compliance causes unreasonable hardship.

headings.title: Equitable balancing of applicant and public interests
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to balance equities between applicant burdens and public environmental impacts.

headings.title: One-year maximum duration and renewal limits for variances
headings.reviewNote: Limits variances to one year and conditions renewals on showing circumstances beyond applicant control.

headings.title: Filing fee and determination of substantive variance petitions
headings.reviewNote: Requires a fifty-dollar fee and department determination whether a variance petition is substantive.

headings.title: Public hearings on substantive variance petitions
headings.reviewNote: Mandates public hearings on substantive variances and upon petitioner request for nonsubstantive petitions.

headings.title: Performance bond requirements ensuring compliance with variance
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to require performance bonds guaranteeing compliance with variance conditions.

headings.title: Revocation or modification of variance or bond upon failure
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to revoke or modify a variance or revoke a bond for noncompliance after a hearing held on at least thirty days written notice.

headings.title: Judicial review rights for final variance decisions
headings.reviewNote: Subjects any commission decision made pursuant to a hearing under this section to judicial review as provided in section 260.415.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsections for 260.405 governing individual hazardous waste variances, petitions, hearings, bonds, revocation or modification, and judicial review.

headings.title: Department duty to investigate alleged hazardous violations
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to investigate alleged violations upon commission request or public complaint.

headings.title: Resolution of violations through conference and conciliation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to resolve identified violations through conference, conciliation, and persuasion.

headings.title: Administrative orders halting violations and emergency directives
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes formal administrative orders halting violations and compelling immediate corrective action.

headings.title: Suspension, revocation, or modification of permits
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes suspending, revoking, or modifying licenses and permits for violations, misrepresentation, or changed conditions; source footnote notes appeal procedure is provided in section 260.415.

headings.title: Hearing rights, counsel representation, and evidence presentation
headings.reviewNote: Grants petitioners rights to counsel, oral argument, witness cross-examination, and evidence presentation.

headings.title: Final commission orders and determinations upon hearing record
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to enter final written orders based on the hearing record or petitioner default.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsections for 260.410 governing violation investigations, conciliation, administrative orders, permit revocations, and appeal hearings.

headings.title: Director authority to issue administrative penalties
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the director to assess administrative penalties for hazardous waste statutory or permit violations.

headings.title: Rulemaking for administrative penalty formulas and caps
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to adopt penalty rules capped at civil limits based on gravity and conduct.

headings.title: Two-year statute of limitations and bar on increases
headings.reviewNote: Requires penalties to be assessed within two years of discovery and bars increases caused by agency delay.

headings.title: Judicial review of administrative penalty orders
headings.reviewNote: Provides that final orders assessing administrative penalties are subject to judicial review under chapter 536.

headings.title: State election between administrative penalty and court action
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the state to elect between administrative penalties and civil court actions for statutory fines.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 260.412 establishing administrative penalties for hazardous waste violations, caps, rules, time limits, and court actions.

headings.title: Judicial review of final commission administrative decisions
headings.reviewNote: Subjects all final commission and department decisions to judicial review under administrative procedure laws.

headings.title: Judicial standard of review for commission regulations
headings.reviewNote: Directs courts to review the administrative record to determine the validity and reasonableness of rules.

headings.title: Preservation of common law and nuisance remedies
headings.reviewNote: Preserves existing common law and statutory remedies for wrongful acts and actions to enjoin nuisances.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 260.415 governing judicial review of final orders, rule validity challenges, and preservation of common law remedies.

headings.title: Emergency administrative orders and civil actions for hazards
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes emergency administrative orders and civil actions to restrain imminent hazards from hazardous wastes.

headings.title: Evidentiary pleading requirements for temporary restraining orders
headings.reviewNote: Requires allegations and proof of substantial danger to health or environment for injunctive relief.

headings.title: Exemption for on-site hazards governed by OSHA
headings.reviewNote: Exempts contained on-site hazards governed by OSHA while preserving department power to prevent escape.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 260.420 authorizing emergency actions against imminent hazards, court injunctions, and OSHA exemptions.

headings.title: Civil penalties and judicial enforcement for violations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes civil actions for injunctive relief and civil penalties up to ten thousand dollars per day.

headings.title: Deposit of penalty moneys into Hazardous Waste Fund
headings.reviewNote: Directs that civil penalties not dedicated to schools by the constitution be deposited in the Hazardous Waste Fund.

headings.title: Criminal offenses and penalties for knowing violations
headings.reviewNote: Punishes knowing illegal transport, treatment, storage, disposal, false statements, tampering, or record destruction by $2,500-$25,000 daily fines and/or up to 1 year county jail for first conviction, and $5,000-$50,000 daily fines and/or at least 10 years imprisonment for subsequent convictions.

headings.title: Sheriff investigation and summons in lieu of arrest
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes requesting sheriff or law enforcement investigations of facility violations and directs officers with probable cause to issue a summons in lieu of arrest, with arrest warrants for failure to appear.

headings.title: Highway patrol detention of equipment and arrest powers
headings.reviewNote: Empowers state highway patrol officers to detain equipment and arrest violators upon probable cause.

headings.title: Liability defense for violations caused by catastrophes
headings.reviewNote: Shields persons from civil penalties if violations result from strikes, acts of God, war, or disasters.

headings.title: Preservation of private civil actions and nuisance suits
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that statutory provisions do not limit private legal actions or nuisance suppression rights.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsections for 260.425 establishing civil penalties, criminal offenses, law enforcement powers, and catastrophe defenses.

headings.title: Public records disclosure and trade secret protections
headings.reviewNote: Makes records public but protects proprietary trade secrets and processes from unlawful disclosure.

headings.title: Preemption of local laws prohibiting permitted facilities
headings.reviewNote: Preempts local laws from barring permitted facilities or transporters except local option on location, establishes a 1/4-mile residential setback without written consent and 300-foot buffer zone, and exempts mining, milling, and smelting wastes.

headings.title: Application of standards to pending facility applications
headings.reviewNote: Requires all pending applicants for hazardous waste disposal facilities to meet all statutory requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 260.430 protecting confidential business trade secrets, preempting local facility bans, and applying rules to pending permits.

headings.title: Mandatory fire and police agreements in unzoned areas

headings.title: Five-year maximum permit term for settlement incinerators
headings.reviewNote: Limits permits for litigation-sited incinerators to five years and bars subsequent renewals.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 260.431 establishing buffer zones, police and fire agreements, and five-year permit limits for incinerators.

headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to establish a program for collecting small quantities of hazardous waste statewide.

headings.title: Free collection limits and fees for excess waste
headings.reviewNote: Directs maximum free collection limits and authorizes cost-reflective fees for additional waste quantities.

headings.title: Department contracts with permitted hazardous waste handlers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department contracts with permitted transporters and handlers for collection operations.

headings.title: Department rulemaking and prohibition on delegating rules
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to adopt program rules and prohibits delegating rulemaking authority to contractors.

headings.title: Safe collection mandate and prohibition on landfill disposal
headings.reviewNote: Guarantees statewide collection access and prohibits landfilling unmanaged exempt small quantity wastes.

headings.reviewNote: Requires annual reassessments categorizing sites into five priority tiers based on health and environmental risk.

headings.title: Removal of properly closed sites from registry

headings.title: Treasurer investment and interest crediting to fund

headings.title: Statutory expiration date for generator disposal fees

headings.title: Comprehensive review and stakeholder proposals for fee structures

headings.title: Director duty to develop state emergency response plan

headings.title: Statewide emergency telephone reporting hotline with technical staff
headings.reviewNote: Requires establishing one statewide emergency telephone number monitored by technical staff capable of advising callers on immediate actions.

headings.title: Immediate interagency notification upon emergency report receipt
headings.reviewNote: Requires the emergency hotline monitor to promptly notify designated response agencies.

headings.title: Mandatory emergency notification duty for persons controlling substances
headings.reviewNote: Requires persons controlling a hazardous substance to notify the state or National Response Center at the earliest practical moment (class A misdemeanor for failure) and bars using notifications in criminal cases except perjury or false statement.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 260.505 directing development of the hazardous substance emergency response plan, statewide emergency hotline, and reporting duties.

headings.title: Director rulemaking authority for hazardous emergencies
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the director to adopt and amend rules implementing emergency response provisions under chapter 536.

headings.title: Prohibition on emergency rules stricter than CERCLA
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits rules stricter than federal Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act rules.

headings.title: Inconsistent state rules declared null and void
headings.reviewNote: Declares inconsistent state regulations null and void, with least stringent federal rules controlling.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 260.520 governing emergency response rulemaking, federal CERCLA stringency limits, and nullification of inconsistent state rules.

headings.title: Strict liability for state hazardous cleanup costs
headings.reviewNote: Imposes strict liability for reasonable state cleanup costs on persons controlling released hazardous substances.

headings.title: Statutory defenses for releases caused by natural acts
headings.reviewNote: Exempts persons from liability if the emergency resulted from an act of God, war, act of Missouri or the United States, or solely a third party (excluding employees, agents, or independent contractors).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 260.530 establishing strict cleanup cost liability to the state and defining statutory defenses.

headings.title: Liability for local emergency response assistance costs
headings.reviewNote: Makes persons controlling released substances liable for reasonable emergency costs incurred by local responders.

headings.title: Thirty-day payment deadline for emergency response cost statements
headings.reviewNote: Requires payment of itemized cost statements within thirty days unless formally contested by written appeal.

headings.title: Director determination on contested cleanup cost appeals
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to resolve contested cost appeals with the burden of proof on the emergency agency.

headings.title: Hazardous Waste Fund reimbursement and mandatory repayment
headings.reviewNote: Allows local responders showing immediate need to obtain reimbursement from the Hazardous Waste Fund and requires them to repay the department upon receiving payment or within the department's deadline even if the responsible party has not paid.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 260.546 establishing emergency response cost liabilities, 30-day payment rules, director appeals, and state fund reimbursement.

headings.title: Liability caps for third-party hazard cleanup contractors
headings.reviewNote: Caps contractor liability for releasing pollutants while abating hazards created by others at $1,000,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence, preserving indemnification rights and excluding intentional, wanton, or willful regulatory violations.

headings.title: Statutory definition of business of waste cleanup
headings.reviewNote: Defines business of waste cleanup of environmental hazard to include investigation, evaluation, planning, design, engineering, removal, construction, and ancillary services; source footnote notes word 'the' appears in original rolls.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 260.552 capping cleanup contractor liability for third-party hazards and defining covered cleanup business services.

headings.title: Creation and custody of Radioactive Waste Investigation Fund

headings.title: Department site investigations upon written local requests
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to conduct scientific investigations upon written requests from local governing bodies, community groups, or individuals, prioritizing receipt order and proximity to federally designated radioactive sites.

headings.title: Investigation execution by agencies or qualified contractors

headings.title: Warrants to access governmental agency property for sampling

headings.title: Reporting sampling results to attorney general and website
headings.reviewNote: Requires reporting final sampling results to the attorney general within forty-five days of receipt and publishing the finalized report and testing results on the department's website.

headings.title: Annual transfer caps, 2025 general revenue shift, and reversion
headings.reviewNote: Caps annual transfers at $150,000, shifts transfers starting August 28, 2025, from the hazardous waste fund to general revenue, reverts unused hazardous waste fund transfers biennially, and retains general revenue and gifts in the fund.

headings.title: State treasurer investment of fund moneys and interest
headings.reviewNote: Directs the state treasurer to invest fund moneys in the same manner as other funds and credit all earned interest and moneys to the fund.

headings.title: Department duty to seek federal reimbursement for testing
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to seek reimbursement of radioactive waste testing expenses from any federal agency responsible for the site.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsections for 260.558 creating the Radioactive Waste Investigation Fund, governing investigation requests, sampling, governmental property warrants, attorney general reports, transfer caps, investments, and federal reimbursement.

headings.title: Department review and notification of application status
headings.reviewNote: Directs department review of voluntary cleanup applications and written notification of acceptance or denial.

headings.reviewNote: Requires submitting all site assessment reports (at minimum a Phase I ESA), sets a 180-day department comment period, and requires posting a deposit up to five thousand dollars by cash or Missouri bank letter of credit.

headings.title: Department approval of additional assessment work plans
headings.reviewNote: Directs department review and approval of work plans when additional site assessments are needed.

headings.title: Department determination of required remedial actions within deadline
headings.reviewNote: Requires department determinations within 180 days specifying necessary remediation or no-further-action status.

headings.title: Remedial action plan contents and ninety-day review
headings.reviewNote: Specifies remedial plan contents including safety and testing plans, with department review within 90 days.

headings.title: Applicant duty to implement approved remedial plans
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicants to faithfully implement approved voluntary remedial action plans.

headings.title: Mandatory quarterly progress reports during remedial implementation
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicants to submit quarterly progress reports on department forms during remediation.

headings.title: Submission of final remedial completion reports to department
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicants to submit copies of all final technical reports regarding voluntary cleanup actions.

headings.title: Department verification review of completed remedial actions
headings.reviewNote: Directs department inspection and verification review of completed remedial actions under approved plans.

headings.title: Applicant right to terminate participation and receive refunds
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes applicants to terminate voluntary participation and receive refunds of unexpended deposit balances.

headings.title: Preservation of department hazardous waste regulatory authorities

headings.title: Administrative appeal rights to Hazardous Waste Commission

headings.title: Deposit of voluntary cleanup reimbursements into fund
headings.reviewNote: Directs deposit of all voluntary cleanup reimbursements into the Hazardous Waste Fund for program use.

headings.title: Department authority to terminate participation for cause

headings.title: Refund or forfeiture of fee balance upon termination

headings.title: Establishment of statewide environmental radiation monitoring program

headings.reviewNote: Bars fund use for non-integral costs, non-dry-cleaning solvent sites, transport releases, fines or penalties, EPA national priorities list sites, noncompliant active facilities, and unreported sites abandoned before July 1, 2009.

headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department personnel and contractors to enter premises upon reasonable notice to perform cleanups.

headings.reviewNote: Excludes bona fide stock purchasers and successors in interest from being treated as the same owner or operator under subsection 7, and denies the section 260.930(5) exemption to operators held liable under subsection 7.

headings.title: Payment duty on solvent sellers regardless of location
headings.reviewNote: Requires the seller or provider of dry-cleaning solvent to pay the surcharge to the department regardless of the seller's or provider's location.

headings.title: Department issuance of solvent surcharge inspection receipts

headings.title: Fifteen percent penalty for nonpayment of surcharges

headings.title: Ten percent annual interest on delinquent surcharges

headings.title: Prohibition on purchasing solvent from nonpaying suppliers
